Submit one toll-free number for verification. The business's details come
from a profile, the kind 10DLC brands use: list yours with
plivo api GET /Profile/ (fields: plivo docs show messaging/api/10dlc/profile).

Usage:
  plivo messaging sms tollfree submit [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help                                help for submit
      --message-volume string               messages a month: 10, 100, 1000, 10000, 100000, 250000, 500000, 750000, 1000000, 5000000 or 10,000,000+ (required)
      --number string                       the toll-free number to verify, E.164 (required)
      --opt-in-image-url string             URL of an image or document that shows the opt-in (required)
      --opt-in-type string                  how recipients opt in: VERBAL|WEB_FORM|PAPER_FORM|VIA_TEXT|MOBILE_QR_CODE (required)
      --privacy-policy-link string          public URL of your privacy policy (required)
      --production-message-content string   sample messages you will send (required)
      --profile-uuid string                 the profile holding the business's details (required)
      --terms-and-conditions-link string    public URL of your terms and conditions (required)
      --use-case string                     use case, or several comma-separated, e.g. 2FA,CUSTOMER_CARE (required)
      --use-case-summary string             how the number's messages are used (required)

Global Flags:
      --dry-run            print the HTTP request without sending
      --log-level string   log level: debug|info|warn|error|none (default "warn")
      --no-color           disable colored output
  -o, --output string      output format: table|json|jsonl|yaml|csv (default: table for TTY, json otherwise)
      --profile string     named profile from ~/.plivo/config.toml
      --query string       JMESPath filter on the JSON output, e.g. 'data.objects[].call_uuid' (implies -o json)
  -q, --quiet              suppress non-data output
      --schema             describe the command (arguments, flags, output fields) instead of running it
      --timeout duration   request timeout: seconds, or a duration such as 90s or 2m (default 30s)
  -y, --yes                skip confirmation prompts
